question: What primary purpose does a postnatal referral system serve in maternal and neonatal health?

options.A: To replace primary health centres with tertiary hospitals completely
options.B: To bridge community health posts and higher levels of care for specialized needs
options.C: To eliminate the need for midwives during the puerperium period
options.D: To increase the duration of hospital stays for every postpartum mother

explanation: A referral system acts as a critical bridge to ensure patients needing specialized care are safely transferred to higher levels of care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the first delay in the three delays model mentioned in the text?

options.A: Delay in deciding to seek care
options.B: Delay in receiving adequate treatment at the facility

explanation: The three delays model includes the delay in deciding to seek care, delay in reaching care, and delay in receiving adequate treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common maternal indication for postnatal referral?

options.C: Normal lochia rubra on day two

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is a severe complication requiring urgent escalation of care and referral. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: Why is early recognition of neonatal indications for referral crucial during the puerperium?

options.A: To prevent minor ailments from progressing into catastrophic emergencies
options.B: To reduce the cost of routine immunizations
options.C: To ensure the mother is discharged early
options.D: To eliminate the need for postnatal home visits

explanation: Catching deviations early prevents minor issues from worsening into life-threatening emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: Which of the following describes a critical postpartum hemorrhage warning sign?

options.A: Spotted lochia serosa on day six
options.B: Soaking through two or more pads per hour for two consecutive hours
options.D: Light staining of blood lasting three days

explanation: Heavy bleeding soaking through two or more pads per hour for two consecutive hours is a clear warning sign of postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h3)

question: What should a midwife do immediately upon identifying a maternal warning sign like high-grade fever with foul-smelling lochia?

options.A: Advise the mother to rest at home and return next week
options.B: Initiate emergency measures and activate the referral protocol
options.C: Wait for spontaneous resolution of symptoms
options.D: Discharge the patient with routine reassurance

explanation: Midwives must initiate emergency life-saving measures and activate the referral protocol immediately upon spotting warning signs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h3)

question: Which finding is considered a neonatal red flag requiring urgent escalation?

options.A: A regular respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute
options.B: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life
options.C: Normal physiological weight loss of 5 percent
options.D: Gentle crying when the infant is hungry

explanation: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is pathological and requires urgent referral. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h4)

question: Why do neonates require especially rapid referral when clinical deterioration is detected?

options.A: They have limited physiological reserves and deteriorate quickly
options.B: They are immune to most postnatal infections
options.C: Their vital signs are impossible to measure accurately
options.D: They recover faster than adult patients without intervention

explanation: Newborns possess limited physiological reserves, meaning delays can rapidly lead to severe outcomes. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h4)

question: Which of the following is a core responsibility of the midwife during a referral?

options.A: Delaying transport until administrative fees are fully paid
options.B: Initiating pre-transfer stabilization and documenting all interventions
options.C: Allowing family members to diagnose the condition before action
options.D: Avoiding communication with the receiving facility to save time

explanation: Midwives must stabilize patients before transfer and maintain meticulous documentation of all care provided. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h5)

question: What role does psychological support play when a midwife prepares a family for a referral?

options.A: It alleviates family anxiety and explains the necessity of the transfer
options.B: It replaces the need for emergency medications
options.C: It lengthens the time required to complete paperwork
options.D: It prevents the patient from being admitted at the receiving hospital

explanation: Offering psychological support helps reduce anxiety and ensures cooperation regarding the urgent transfer. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of pre-referral stabilization before transporting a patient?

options.A: To delay transport until routine lab results are finalized
options.B: To sustain the patient's vital functions and physiological state during transit
options.C: To avoid notifying the receiving health centre
options.D: To eliminate the need for a skilled escort during travel

explanation: Stabilization ensures that the patient's condition is supported and managed to withstand the journey to the receiving facility. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h6)

question: Which intervention is appropriate for pre-referral stabilization of a compromised newborn?

options.A: Placing the infant in a cold room to reduce metabolic rate
options.B: Withholding all feeds and fluids indefinitely
options.C: Preventing hypothermia through thermal care like skin-to-skin contact
options.D: Delaying airway clearance until arrival at the hospital

explanation: Preventing hypothermia through thermal care is vital for stabilizing a compromised newborn before transport. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h6)

question: What does the SBAR communication tool stand for in clinical handovers?
explanation: SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation, ensuring structured and effective communication. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h7)

question: Why must a formal referral form accompany the patient to the receiving facility?

options.A: To serve as a souvenir for the patient's family
options.B: To provide clinical details, vital signs, and treatments administered to prevent fragmented care
options.C: To allow the receiving facility to charge extra administrative fees
options.D: To replace the need for a verbal handover from the midwife

explanation: The referral form provides vital clinical details and treatment history to ensure continuity of care without duplication. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h7)

question: Which of the following represents a major structural barrier to effective referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed ambulances in rural areas
options.B: Poor road infrastructure and transport delays
options.C: Universal free healthcare for all postpartum mothers
options.D: Immediate availability of specialized care at every village health post

explanation: Poor road networks and transport difficulties are prominent structural barriers hindering timely referrals in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h8)

question: How can midwives help overcome cultural and community barriers to formal healthcare referrals?

options.A: By ignoring community practices and isolating patients
options.B: Through community mobilization, health education, and advocacy
options.C: By encouraging reliance solely on traditional birth attendants
options.D: By charging higher fees for emergency services

explanation: Midwives overcome community barriers by engaging in health education, community mobilization, and advocacy. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h8)
